To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the composition of local government workforces has changed, that there has not been a strategic alignment of HRM practices to organisational goals, and that the management of temporary staff, independent and external contractors, volunteers and work placement students has been ad hoc.

the composition of the workforce in Victoria’s local governments is complex, that there has not been a systematic approach to workforce planning in the sector, and that there is little evidence that councils have used theories of strategic human resource management to manage their workforces.
Local government in Victoria has a workforce which is more complex and more diverse than previously recognised.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the management of the ‘known’ workforce, but the ‘hidden’ workforce remains largely unmanaged.
the ‘missing workforce’ of local government.
the ‘known and managed’ workforce, but also with a significant ‘hidden workforce’ that councils have little knowledge of and which is not managed strategically.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is little evidence of strategic HRM practices in relation to the workforce in Victorian local government.
there is a need to better understand, and to strategically align, the management of the workforce in Victorian local government.
the workforce in local government is not being strategically managed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there is a need for a more comprehensive approach to workforce planning and management in local government.
councils are not strategically managing their external workforce, and that this is a major gap in council HRM.
councils have not strategically managed the workforce.
The main takeaway from our work is that
councils need to develop a workforce strategy which includes all the staff they use.
councils need to develop a more strategic approach to their workforces, and to recognise that they have a broader workforce than is often acknowledged.
councils have a large, diverse, external workforce, and there is a need for more research to understand how this workforce is managed, and the impact of this on council performance.
